title: What Mike Vrabel said about his viral challenge flag toss
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Mike Vrabel plans to retain his challenge flag duties despite NFL rule changes allowing delegation to another staffer.
Vrabel's high-arc challenge flag toss in the Patriots' preseason game against the Colts went viral on social media.
Vrabel successfully challenged a ruling during the game, helping the Patriots gain a fumble recovery over the Colts.

title: 16 hospitalized after chemical incident at Mass. industrial worksite
author: Audrey Cooney
bullets: Sixteen employees were hospitalized after falling ill during a chemical incident at an industrial site in Hudson, Massachusetts.
The Hudson Fire Department responded at 8:45 a.m. after an employee pulled a fire alarm due to symptoms.
Firefighters from Marlborough, Stowe, Maynard, and Berlin provided mutual aid during the incident response.

title: 2 New England spots make NYT’s list of best Mexican restaurants
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: New York Times named Food Truck Paradise in New Haven, CT and Tuxpan Taqueria in Central Falls, RI among best U.S. Mexican eateries.
Food Truck Paradise features 28 diverse food trucks, with Mexican vendors specializing in unique beverages like avocado slushies and mangonadas.
Tuxpan Taqueria, known for its standout tacos and specialties, was a 2023 James Beard Semifinalist for Best New Restaurant.

title: Are tire rotations necessary for electric vehicles?
author: John Paul
bullets: Electric vehicles, such as the Nissan Leaf, wear tires faster due to instant torque and added weight.
Regular tire rotations maximize tread life and reduce noise in electric vehicles, even if tires wear evenly.
Tire life in electric vehicles is shorter compared to gasoline vehicles due to low-rolling-resistance tires.

title: Patriots place Terrell Jennings on IR, sign two more running backs
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots place running back Terrell Jennings on injured reserve with an undisclosed injury, impacting their running back competition.
Patriots sign JaMychal Hasty and Hasan Haskins to bolster running back depth after placing Jennings on injured reserve.
Myles Montgomery also placed on injured reserve as Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson lead the running back chart.

title: Celtics release 2026-27 schedule: When will Jaylen Brown return to Boston?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Celtics will start their 2026-27 season with an October 20 game against the Detroit Pistons.
Jaylen Brown, now with the 76ers, will return to Boston to face the Celtics on January 21, 2027.
The Celtics will host reigning NBA champions New York Knicks in their home opener on October 23 at TD Garden.

title: Payton Tolle pitches 8-inning gem as Red Sox end 5-game skid with 7-0 win over Blue Jays
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Rookie Payton Tolle pitched eight innings allowing two hits, helping the Red Sox end a five-game losing streak.
Caleb Durbin hit a grand slam in the eighth inning, breaking open the game against the Blue Jays.
Boston remains in position for an AL wild-card playoff berth despite matching their worst season skid.

title: 7 takeaways from Patriots’ 13-13 tie with Colts in preseason opener
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots opened their preseason with a 13-13 tie against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium.
Veteran defenders Kindle Vildor, Jeremiah Pharms Jr., and K. J. Britt contributed to four turnovers against the Colts.
Injuries affected the Patriots' offensive line, with Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich both leaving the game due to leg injuries.

title: Cape Cod documentarian Mischa Richter creates a dreamy ode to Grateful Dead culture with ‘Summer Tour’
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Mischa Richter's documentary 'Summer Tour' explores Grateful Dead culture and Deadheads' nomadic lifestyle during Dead & Co.'s final tour.
'Summer Tour' follows young Deadheads Jerry Pierce and Annie Dunn as they travel across the country, illustrating community and idealism.
Richter co-produced with longtime friend Chloë Sevigny; the film screened at Telluride and will have local showings in New England.

title: Tiffani Faison to close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool’s Errand in the Fenway
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Tiffani Faison will close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool's Errand in Fenway, ending Sweet Cheeks' 15-year run on November 24.
Sweet Cheeks and Fool's Errand closures are driven by high operational costs in Boston's unsustainable restaurant environment.
Faison seeks a new location for Sweet Cheeks and plans to relocate affected employees within her Big Heart Hospitality group.
